Use a straight horizontal 100 m long pipe with an internal diameter of 50 mm.
Use a volumetric flow rate of 2 L/s, equivalent to 0.002 m³/s.
Use water properties at 20°C with rho = 998 kg/m³ and mu = 1e-3 Pa·s.
Use galvanized iron absolute roughness epsilon = 0.15 mm.
Calculate cross-sectional area A = pi D² / 4 = 0.0019635 m².
Calculate velocity V = Q / A = 1.0186 m/s.
Calculate Reynolds number Re = rho V D / mu = 50,830.
Use the Darcy friction factor with epsilon/D = 0.003, giving f = 0.0289.
Calculate pressure drop ΔP = f (L/D) (rho V² / 2) = 29.9 kPa.
Assume no fittings, no elevation change, and fully developed turbulent flow.
The pressure drop is approximately 30 kPa, or 0.30 bar.
